Add a mix of “browns,” such as dry leaves, shredded paper, and cardboard, and “greens,” such as fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, and grass clippings. Aim for roughly two or three parts browns to one part greens, and keep the mixture about as damp as a wrung-out sponge. Turn or stir it every week or two to add air. Avoid meat, fish, dairy, oily foods, pet waste, and diseased plants, since these can attract pests or create odors. When the compost becomes dark, crumbly, and earthy-smelling, it is ready to use in gardens or around plants.
